plan: In a sealed-bid second-price auction with independent private values, the weakly dominant strategy is to bid your true value. Your bid only determines whether you win; the price paid is the second-highest bid. Overbidding risks winning at a price above your value; underbidding risks losing when winning would be profitable. With no informative history and uniform values in [0,49], bidding truthfully maximizes expected profit this round and in general. Therefore, bid exactly your value: 35.

[ With independent private values and a second‑price rule, the weakly dominant strategy is to bid my true value. Truthful bidding guarantees I win exactly when my value is the highest and I pay the second-highest bid, maximizing expected profit. Shading risks losing profitable wins; overbidding risks winning at a price above value, yielding negative profit. There’s no past history to adjust for, and values are redrawn i.i.d. this round. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of 32, in $0.1 increments allowed (32.0 is valid). ]

[ In a sealed-bid second-price auction with independent private values, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy. Overbidding risks winning when the second-highest bid exceeds your value, causing negative profit; underbidding risks losing when you would have gained. With value 48 and bids in $0.1 increments, I will bid exactly 48 to maximize expected profit. Ties break randomly; bidding higher doesn’t improve payment, only win probability, and truthful already optimizes that tradeoff. ]
